user_questions.question: What counts as a failing grade that should suspend a storefront? Options: (a) a grade picklist such as A, B, C, Fail where Fail suspends (recommended; no grade field exists in the org today); (b) a numeric score threshold, e.g. score below 70 suspends (please give the number); (c) a letter scale A-F where F suspends. Evidence: the org has no inspection object, grade, or score field; Storefront__c.Status__c already has the value Suspended.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Grade A/B/C/Fail; Fail sets the storefront to Suspended.

skill_friction: AskCoworker's wrong claims were mostly platform claims (validation rules and flow bodies 'not queryable', workflow master-detail limit, Task object permissions); the 2-wrong/4-wrong thresholds counted these the same as fact errors, and after 4 it was unclear whether skipping T after R had already run was the intent (I skipped T).
Split-retry accounting: a split sends two calls but counts as one retry; run.json has no kind to distinguish the two halves, so both were recorded as 'retry'.

Design rule 'include a notification to the record owner when a change leaves records needing human follow-up' conflicts in spirit with 'drop behavior nobody asked for'; it is unclear whether a suspension qualifies. I included a Task.
Master-detail sharing setting (writeRequiresMasterRead) and required-ness of fields on a brand-new object with no writers are not covered by the 'data shape' rule; decided as assumptions.

The R/T template says to split R into runtime and security halves only for more than 6 changes; with 11 changes the first combined R call should have been split up front, which I missed and cost a timeout.
